title: A role change signs the user out before a status change goes through
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a custom role for this test, role D, with Part Library & Inventory — View, Part Library & Inventory — Create & Edit, Part Library & Inventory — Delete and See Financial Data, and with no Vendor Order Management, Part Sales or Settings permission, so user D starts with the right to delete parts.
  • Create a staff member for this test, user D, at the test location with role D.
  • Use two browser windows: window 1 signed in as the Admin, window 2 (a private window) signed in as user D.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test.
  • Start window 1 on role D's Edit Role page (Roles & Permissions), with nothing changed yet.
  • Start window 2 on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. In window 2, click the three-dot actions button (⋮).
  2. In window 2, click Deactivate parts.
  3. In window 2, click the part A row.
  4. In window 2, click Deactivate on the dark bar.
  5. In window 1, untick Part Library & Inventory — Create & Edit.
  6. In window 1, untick Part Library & Inventory — Delete.
  7. In window 1, untick See Financial Data.
  8. In window 1, untick every permission in the Settings group.
  9. In window 1, click Save.
  10. In window 2, click Deactivate in the confirmation.
  11. In window 1, click Parts in the top bar.
  12. In window 1, click Inventory in the left menu.
  13. In window 1, type part A's part number in the Search box.
  14. In window 2, sign in as user D.
  15. In window 2, click Parts in the top bar.
  16. In window 2, click Inventory in the left menu.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The menu opens for user D and lists Deactivate parts.

Step 2:

  • Bulk mode turns on.

Step 3:

  • The bar reads 1 selected.

Step 4:

  • The "Deactivate parts?" confirmation opens. Leave it open: the old controls stay on screen until user D's next action.

Step 5:

  • The Create & Edit box is unticked.

Step 6:

  • The Delete box is unticked.

Step 7:

  • The See Financial Data box is unticked.

Step 8:

  • Every Settings permission is unticked.

Step 9:

  • Role D is saved with only Part Library & Inventory — View left in the Part Library and Inventory group: user D now cannot delete inventory parts.

Step 10:

  • In window 2 the message "Session expired, please log in again." appears and user D is signed out: the role change ended the session at user D's next action.
  • No "1 part updated." message appears.

Step 11:

  • Window 1 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 12:

  • Window 1 shows the Inventory page on the Active tab.

Step 13:

  • Part A is still listed on the Active tab: its status did not change.

Step 14:

  • User D is signed in again in window 2.

Step 15:

  • Window 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 16:

  • The Inventory page opens for user D with no three-dot actions button (⋮) in the toolbar: after signing in again the screen follows the new role, which has View only.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10821 (Story 8, Permissions)

  • S8-R15: “The system accepts a status change, a tracking change and an untracked part from exactly the users it accepts an inventory part delete from today.”
  • S8-R3: “A user without that permission does not see the "Deactivate parts" entry in the Inventory actions menu.”
  • S8-R5: “The actions menu needs the 'Part Library & Inventory → Create & Edit' permission. Its Cycle count and Export entries need nothing more. Only the bulk status entry also needs the 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' permission.”

From: Product's answers to questions 13 to 27 (Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, Google Doc https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pkAPGqWVTdtYorNN4SVNl9HkHxuuB9czro_y2DbUeEM/edit, saved word for word in full-pass-2026-10-27/ANSWERS-13-27-2026-10-27.md), read 28 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 27: “Changing a user's role logs that user out on their next action, with "Session expired, please log in again." Until then the old controls stay on screen. After logging back in, they follow the new role.”
  • Chris Ward, 27 Oct 2026, answer 27: “For S8-N1 to S8-N3, use a role without Part Library & Inventory Create & Edit, Vendor Order Management Create & Edit, Part Sales Delete, Settings Parts or See financial data.”
